name: Siena
description: From one of the country's most beautiful Gothic cathedrals to an exciting urban horserace, life in this UNESCO-listed hilltop city revolves around the central square.

name: Ragusa
description: For centuries, this UNESCO World Heritage Site was two separate cities, meaning its doubly full of beautiful Baroque architecture.

description: The traditional, cone-roofed 'Trulli' houses in this picturesque village are so distinctive, they're a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Naples
description: Food lovers will rejoice as they explore Naples, the city of pasta, coffee, and most importantly, pizza.

name: La Spezia
description: Since the days of the Roman Empire La Spezia has been one of the region's most important ports and trade centers. It's also home to Italy's largest naval base. Many travelers overlook that it also has an atmospheric Old Town and is a great base for exploring the surrounding area. Walking the narrow lanes, it's still possible to see architectural elements ranging from engraved 14th century portals to double lancet windows, baroque pediments, and embellishments often seen on Renaissance palaces. The Basilica of Santa Maria Assunta offers a survey of changing architectural styles as it took 600 years to fully complete. For a more nuanced look at Italian history, head to the 13th century San Giorgio Castle, which has an archaeological museum with artefacts dating back to the Copper Age. The Naval Technical Museum offers fascinating insights into Italian naval history with fantastic displays like cannons, dive suits, model ships, and control panels from battleships.

name: Cefalu
description: With one of Sicily's finest beaches, and a UNESCO-listed cathedral, this picturesque medieval village is a coastal jewel.

name: Modena
description: Modena, a town known for its architectural gems and contributions to the art of cooking, is also home to the famous sports car—the Ferrari.

name: Padua
description: Home to Italy's second oldest university, the 14th-century frescoes scattered throughout this ancient city make up a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Agrigento
description: Sitting above the UNESCO-listed Valley of the Temples, modern Agrigento has a criminally overlooked historic center.

name: Ravello
description: With its sweeping views and luscious gardens, this UNESCO-listed town has conquered the hearts of many artists and intellectuals.

name: Ravenna
description: Ravenna has one of the most impressive collections of Christian mosaic artwork, deemed of the utmost importance once Ravenna joined the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1996.

name: Polignano a Mare

name: Matera

name: Bellagio
description: This charming town and its many beautiful villas sits directly on the water between the two branches of Lake Como.

name: Parma
description: Located in the northern Italian region of Emilia-Romagna lies the elegant city of Parma, famous for its gastronomy, architecture, and music.

name: Noto
description: This UNESCO-listed city is abloom with elegant Baroque monuments.

name: Lecce
description: From Roman ruins to distinctive Baroque architecture, this ancient city is an architectural gem.

name: Venice
description: It's hard to decide which is more stunning: Venice's historic architecture, or the network of canals running through it.

name: Turin
description: Once the home to Italy's royal family, the House of Savoy, Turin is a magnificent city with various artworks from the Renaissance to Art Nouveau periods.

name: Taormina
description: Sicily's premier holiday destination is an intoxicating mix of natural beauty and ancient history.

name: Positano
description: With its jumble of pastel-colored houses cascading down a cliff to the sea, it's no wonder this romantic resort town is known as the "postcard of the Amalfi Coast".

name: Bologna
description: This medieval town in northern Italy is famed for its lively student population, impeccable cuisine, theatre, and nightlife.

name: Verona
description: Fair Verona isn't just the setting for Romeo and Juliet; it's a tragically enchanting riverside city.

name: Bergamo
description: This alluring city has the classic Italian fair of beautiful buildings and red roofs, but its trademark feature has a rare twist with an elegant charm.

name: Sorrento

name: Ferrara
description: Europe's first modern city, Ferrara is a spectacular metropolis of art and culture. It blends medieval and Renaissance for a distinctive combination.

name: Trieste
description: The charming city and seaport of Trieste lies between Latin, Germanic, and Slavic lands. It's surrounded by hills on one side and the Mediterranean on the other. This underrated and often overlooked city has a vibrant, culturally diverse atmosphere with an Eastern-European feel.

name: San Gimignano

name: Mantua
description: An often overlooked Renaissance gem, the city of Mantova was chosen as the Italian Capital of Culture in 2016.

name: Genoa
description: Italy's largest seaport, the birthplace of Christopher Columbus is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with one of Europe's biggest historic centers and over 100 opulent palaces.

name: Milan
description: Milan is one of the major fashion capitals of the world with fashion, elegance, and money at its core.

name: Portofino

description: Southeast of Genoa, this photogenic city was once a haven for Genoa's growing merchant marine fleet before becoming an aristocratic escape.

description: In the southern part of the Alps within Italy's border, lies Cortina d'Ampezzo, a winter wonderland with over a 1,000 years of history.

name: Rome
description: According to Roman mythology, Rome was founded by Romulus in 753 BC after killing his brother Remus over a dispute on which hill their city should be built on. Called the "Eternal City" for its long history, and the "City of Seven Hills", Rome's nicknames give a clue what to expect. Now home to nearly 3 million people, the Eternal City's long history is well-preserved in its many monuments and museums. Head to the UNESCO-listed city center to find most of Rome's most iconic monuments, like the Colosseum, Foro Romano, and Palatino. Along with its many ancient monuments, Rome was a major Renaissance center and the birthplace of the Baroque style and Neoclassicism. The Trevi Fountain, Sistine Chapel with Michaelangelo's famous ceiling, and Saint Peter's Basilica are all masterpieces. Save time for Rome's museums, like the Vatican Museums, the Musei Capitolini, the Borghese Gallery, and the Palazzo Barberini Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica to see the works of Masters up close.

name: Pisa
description: Straddling the River Arno, the Italian city of Pisa has much more to offer than its famous Leaning Tower.

name: Florence
